newsitem.title: UK: St Paul seeks buyer for UK's Minet-analysts.
newsitem.headline: St Paul seeks buyer for UK's Minet-analysts.

text.p: St Pauls Cos' announcement that it had retained Goldman Sachs to consider the future of its UK insurance broker Minet was tantamount to putting a for sale board outside the company, analysts said.
"Presumably it means find a buyer or organise an MBO (management buy-out)," one UK insurance analyst, who asked not to be named, told Reuters on Tuesday.
St. Pauls said earlier it had retained Goldman Sachs International to assist in examining strategic alternatives for its Minet Group insurance brokerage operation.
A spokeswoman for Minet in London said, "There's nothing else I can add to what the press release said...St Pauls is looking at various options."
Another analyst said St Pauls, which acquired Minet in 1988, had been seeking a buyer for some time.
"A while ago there was strong feeling that Aon was going to take it off their hands, but clearly that's not going to happen, hence the announcement about Goldman."
Analysts said they could not altogether rule out the possibility that Minet may be merged or sold off piece meal, but considered these outcomes unlikely.
"I can't really see that many options. They could merge it with someone else, but this sort of announcement is generally code that they're looking for a trade sale," a third analyst said.
Minet was recently ranked the world's ninth largest broker and number four in the UK, leaving only a small number of potential trade buyers large enough to finance its acquisition.
Alexander & Alexander was a possibility, analysts said, but added that a bid from the two largest UK brokers -- Sedgwick and Willis Corroon -- was unlikely.
Minet had revenue of $367 million in the year to end September, 1995, 4,000 employees and more than 125 offices worldwide.

St Pauls described the second quarter earnings of Minet for the current year as disappointing. Last year it made a pre-tax $13.1 million loss after a $10 million loss in 1994 and a $13 million loss in 1993.
In July, Minet pulled out of the North American retail energy and marine sector with the closure of four offices.
The St. Pauls Cos provide property-casualty insurance underwriting and insurance brokerage products and services worldwide.
